content.value_statement: Investment teams need repeatable valuation analysis with transparent assumptions. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code build DCF models, test sensitivities, and compare scenarios.
actual_capabilities: Builds DCF projections from historical revenue, EBITDA, capex, working capital, and growth assumptions.
Calculates WACC using risk-free rate, beta, market premium, debt cost, leverage, and tax rate.
Computes enterprise value with terminal growth or exit multiple methods.
Calculates equity value and per-share valuation from net debt, cash, and shares outstanding.
Runs one-way, two-way, tornado, breakeven, and scenario sensitivity analyses.
Produces pandas DataFrames and text summaries for valuation outputs.
limitations: Does not fetch live market data or verify financial statements automatically.
Monte Carlo simulation is documented but not implemented in the included Python files.
Outputs depend on user-supplied assumptions and require professional review.
Example scripts may need adaptation for tax, accounting, or sector rules.

use_cases.title: Evaluate an Acquisition
use_cases.description: Estimate enterprise and equity value, then test WACC and growth assumptions for an acquisition target.

use_cases.title: Plan a Capital Project
use_cases.description: Compare project scenarios with different operating assumptions and probability weights.

use_cases.title: Review Valuation Risk
use_cases.description: Rank valuation drivers with tornado analysis and identify breakeven assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Base DCF
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a base DCF model for this company using the attached financials. Show assumptions, WACC, enterprise value, equity value, and key checks.

prompt_templates.title: Test Key Assumptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Run sensitivity analysis on revenue growth, EBITDA margin, WACC, and terminal growth. Rank the largest valuation drivers and explain the range.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Planning Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Create best, base, and downside scenarios for this investment case. Use probability weights and summarize expected value, upside, and downside risk.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Investment Case
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this financial model for assumption quality, valuation sensitivity, breakeven thresholds, and unsupported conclusions. List recommended model changes.

output_examples.input: Build a DCF for a software company with five years of projections.
output: A projection summary with revenue, EBITDA, taxes, capex, working capital, and free cash flow.
A WACC calculation with cost of equity, cost of debt, and capital structure assumptions.
An enterprise value and equity value summary with value per share.

output_examples.input: Show how valuation changes when WACC and terminal growth move.
output: A two-way sensitivity table comparing valuation across WACC and terminal growth ranges.
A short explanation of which assumption drives the largest change.
A warning where assumptions create unrealistic or unstable outputs.

output_examples.input: Compare upside, base, and downside cases for a project.
output: A scenario comparison table with assumptions, probabilities, outputs, and weighted value.
A concise interpretation of upside potential, downside exposure, and expected value.

best_practices: Document every assumption source before running valuation outputs.
Use multiple valuation methods when the decision depends on a single model result.
Stress test WACC, growth, margin, and terminal value assumptions before presenting conclusions.
anti_patterns: Do not present model output as investment advice.
Do not use default assumptions when company-specific data is available.
Do not ignore accounting, tax, regulatory, or sector-specific adjustments.

faq.question: What financial models does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports DCF valuation, sensitivity analysis, breakeven analysis, and probability-weighted scenario comparison.

faq.question: Can it calculate WACC?
faq.answer: Yes. It can calculate WACC from risk-free rate, beta, market premium, debt cost, leverage, and tax rate.

faq.question: Does it fetch live market data?
faq.answer: No. You need to provide market inputs, company financials, and assumption ranges.

faq.question: Can it create Monte Carlo simulations?
faq.answer: The documentation discusses Monte Carlo analysis, but the included Python files do not implement it.

faq.question: Is this a substitute for professional financial advice?
faq.answer: No. Outputs are analytical support and require professional review before any investment decision.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
